card.title: 51e RÉGIMENT
card.text: Deployment: Choose One - Gain +3 attack and Blitz OR gain +3 defense and Guard.
card.flavorText: The 51st Infantry Regiment is a unit of the French Army created in 1791, under the Revolution. It took part in several major battles against the enemies of France throughout History, notably during the Napoleonic Wars, the Crimean War, the Second French intervention in Mexico and the Great War. At the dawn of World War 2, the regiment was part of the 3rd Motorized Infantry Division and used as backup for the French Second Army, which was charged with preventing the Germans from outflanking the Maginot Line at the South of the Belgian border. During the German invasion, they participated in the Battle of Stonne, one of the largest fights in the Battle of France, sometimes referred to as “1940’s Verdun”. From May 15th to May 27th, 42,500 French soldiers and 130 French tanks, facing 90,000 German soldiers and 300 German tanks, fought violently in and around the village of Stonne, located on a crest dominating the German breakthrough’s spearhead at Sedan. The village changed hands 17 times in only 3 days. Largely outnumbered, and despite managing to inflict significant losses and to slow down the Germans, the French lost the battle and ultimately failed in their attempt to stop the enemy moving forward to the sea and cutting their forces in half. After the fall of France, the 51st Infantry Regiment became part of the Armistice Army (or Vichy French Army) until its dissolution in November 1942 when the German forces invaded the Free Zone and occupied all of France. The unit was reformed after the Allies landed in Provence, and was engaged in the Dunkirk Pocket, where 10,000 heavily equipped and determined German soldiers resisted from September 1944 to the German surrender in May 1945.
